simple.meaning: אַחַר (ʼachar) is a Hebrew object word meaning “after.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Daniel 2:29. The surrounding context includes kingship, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַחַר (H311) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אַחַר (ʼachar) / H311 is traced through Daniel 2:29, Daniel 2:45, Daniel 7:24 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “As for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what will happen.

timeline.evidenceText: “As for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what will happen.

Because you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it broke in pieces the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God has made known to the king what will happen hereafter. The dream is certain, and its interpretation sure.”
As for the ten horns, ten kings will arise out of this kingdom. Another will arise after them; and he will be different from the former, and he will put down three kings.

definitions.full: H311. achar [ אחר ] plural with אַחֲרֵי , preposition after (Cappadocian and Egyptian Aramaic אחר afterwards (Lzb Eph.i. 361 S-C pap C 8 ), probably Nabataean אחר after (Lzb 212 SAC 16 ); Egyptian Aramaic אחריכם (S-C Pap. c 8 +); ᵑ7 (sometimes) אֲחוֺרֵי ; Biblical Hebrew אַחַר ); — דְנָה אַחֲרֵי after this Dan 2:29 , 45 ; with suffix אַחֲרֵיהֹן 7:24 . Usu. Aramaic synonym בָּאתַר , q. v.
